lessons.title: Greetings & how are you
lessons.goal: I can greet someone at the right time of day, say how I am, and get through a lesson with please, thank you, sorry and "say that again".

learn.title: Hello, by time of day
learn.jp: おはよう・こんにちは・こんばんは
learn.intro: Japanese greetings change with the clock. Morning, daytime and evening each have their own word, and the morning one has a casual and a polite form.

rule.label: Three greetings
rule.pattern: おはよう(ございます) → morning ／ こんにちは → daytime ／ こんばんは → evening
rule.note: Add ございます to おはよう for anyone who isn't a close friend. こんにちは and こんばんは are written with は but said "wa".

learn.when: Walking into a lesson, a shop, a meeting. Before anything else.
tips: The は at the end of こんにちは is the topic particle ("as for today..."), which is why it's spelled は but read wa.
There's no "hi" for any time of day. Pick the one that matches the clock.

learn.title: How are you?
learn.intro: げんき means well, lively, in good spirits. Add ですか and it's the question; answer with the same word plus です.

rule.label: Ask and answer
rule.pattern: げんきですか？ → げんきです。 ／ （ちょっと）つかれています。
rule.note: The answer echoes the question. ちょっと (a little) softens anything. つかれています = I'm tired (an ongoing state).

learn.when: Right after hello. Your teacher asks it every lesson, so have an answer ready.

examples.jp: しゅうまつは ゆっくりします。
examples.en: I'll take it easy this weekend.

tips: After answering, ask back with the person's name: げんきです。ゆうやさんは？ That's a conversation, not an interview.

learn.title: Thank you, please, sorry
learn.jp: ありがとう・おねがいします・すみません
learn.intro: Four words carry most of everyday politeness. Two of them, すみません and どうぞ, do several jobs each.

rule.label: The polite four
rule.pattern: ありがとう(ございます) ／ おねがいします ／ すみません ／ どうぞ
rule.note: ございます makes thank-you polite. おねがいします is "please" when asking for something. すみません is excuse me, sorry and thank-you-for-the-trouble. どうぞ is go ahead / here you are.

learn.when: Getting attention in a shop: すみません. Ordering: おねがいします. Handing something over: どうぞ.

examples.jp: ありがとう（ございます）。
examples.en: Thank you. (polite with ございます)

tips: If you learn one word for Japan, make it すみません. It opens every interaction with a stranger.

learn.title: Inside a lesson
learn.intro: These keep a lesson moving when you're lost. Saying them in Japanese, instead of switching to English, is itself practice.

rule.label: Asking for help
rule.pattern: もういちど おねがいします ／ ちょっと まって ください ／ わかりました ／ わかりません
rule.note: ください after a verb = please do it (まって ください, きいて ください). わかりました = got it; わかりません = I don't understand.

learn.when: Missed something: もういちど おねがいします. Need a second: ちょっと まって ください. Understood: わかりました.

examples.jp: もういちど おねがいします。
ちょっと まって ください。

examples.en: I don't understand. / I don't know.

tips: わかりました (past) means "it has become clear": you say it once you understand. わかります on its own is rarer.

learn.title: Reacting
learn.jp: いいですね・よかったです
learn.intro: Short reactions make you sound like a listener instead of a dictionary. All of them end in です, and most take ね.

rule.label: React with ね
rule.pattern: いいですね ／ おいしいですね ／ よかったです
rule.note: ね invites the other person to agree: "nice, isn't it?". よかったです (it was good) is the past of いい.

learn.when: Someone tells you a plan: いいですね. Food: おいしいですね. Looking back on something: よかったです.

examples.jp: きょうの レッスンは よかったです。
examples.romaji: kyou no ressun wa yokatta desu

examples.jp: きょうは どうでしたか？

tips: Say いいですね a lot. It's the single most useful reaction in Japanese.

learn.title: Saying goodbye
learn.intro: じゃあね is the casual "see you". With a teacher or someone older, add polite thanks before it.

rule.label: Leaving
rule.pattern: じゃあね。 ／ ありがとうございました。
rule.note: じゃあね is for friends and friendly teachers. さようなら is formal and sounds final; you'll rarely need it.

learn.when: End of a lesson, leaving a shop, hanging up.

examples.jp: ありがとう（ございます）。
examples.en: Thank you. (polite with ございます)

tips: Your teacher ends with きょうの レッスンは よかったです。じゃあね。 You can say the same back.

build.why: ございます makes おはよう polite. Use it with anyone who isn't a close friend.
Spelled は, said wa. It's the topic particle hiding inside the greeting.
Echo the question: げんきですか → げんきです. Drop the か.

build.jp: ちょっと つかれて___。
build.why: つかれています is an ongoing state: I'm (currently) tired.
きいて + ください = please listen. ください asks someone to do the verb.
もういちど = one more time. おねがいします = please.
ちょっと (a moment) + まって (wait) + ください (please).
ません is the polite negative. わかりました would mean the opposite: got it.
いい (good) + です + ね (isn't it).
よかった already carries the past tense. です just makes it polite.
きょうの レッスン = today's lesson (の links them). Then は, then the comment.
すみません gets attention, apologises and thanks.
どうぞ when handing something over or letting someone go first.

build.en: I'll take it easy this weekend.
build.why: Topic (しゅうまつは) first, verb (します) last.
じゃあね is the casual goodbye.
どう = how. どうでしたか = how was it?

speak.jp: こんにちは。
おはようございます。
こんばんは。
げんきですか？
げんきです。
（ちょっと）つかれています。

speak.en: Thank you. (polite with ございます)
speak.jp: ありがとう（ございます）。
すみません。
もういちど おねがいします。
ちょっと まって ください。
わかりました。

speak.en: I don't understand. / I don't know.
speak.jp: わかりません。
いいですね。
きょうは どうでしたか？
よかったです。
じゃあね。

lessons.title: Introducing yourself
lessons.goal: I can introduce myself (name, where I'm from, job, hobby, goal) and ask what something is.

learn.title: The introduction sandwich
learn.jp: はじめまして・よろしく
learn.intro: Every Japanese self-introduction starts and ends with a fixed phrase. Learn the two ends, and you can put anything in the middle.

rule.label: Opener and closer
rule.pattern: はじめまして。 … よろしく おねがいします。
rule.note: はじめまして = nice to meet you (first meeting only). よろしく おねがいします = please treat me well; it closes the introduction and has no real English equivalent.

learn.when: Meeting anyone for the first time. The other person says both lines back.

examples.jp: よろしく おねがいします。
examples.en: Nice to meet you. / Please treat me well.

tips: Bow slightly on よろしく おねがいします. The phrase and the bow go together.

learn.title: Name, place, job
learn.jp: エランです・フロリダから きました
learn.intro: Three facts, three short sentences. All of them are X は Y です or end in a verb, and the subject (I) is usually left out.

rule.label: Who you are
rule.pattern: （ぼくは）エランです。 ／ フロリダから きました。 ／ ぼくは オフィスマネージャーです。
rule.note: から = from. きました = came. ぼく is "I" for men in casual-polite speech; わたし works for anyone.

learn.when: After はじめまして. Name first, then where from, then what you do.

examples.jp: フロリダから きました。
ぼくは オフィスマネージャーです。

tips: Katakana words are borrowed: フロリダ (Florida), オフィスマネージャー (office manager). Say them with Japanese vowels: fu-ro-ri-da.

learn.title: Hobby and goal
learn.intro: Hobby and goal are the two questions you'll be asked most. Both use X は Y です with the question word なん in the Y slot.

rule.label: Ask and answer
rule.pattern: しゅみは なんですか？ → しゅみは おんがくです。
rule.note: なん = what. Put it where the answer goes, add か. The answer swaps なん for the real thing.

learn.when: Getting to know someone. Also your teacher's favourite warm-up question.

examples.jp: しゅみは なんですか？
しゅみは おんがくです。
もくひょうは にほんりょこうです。
examples.en: My goal is a trip to Japan.

examples.jp: すきな たべものは なんですか？
examples.romaji: suki na tabemono wa nan desu ka?

examples.jp: すきな たべものは すしです。
examples.romaji: suki na tabemono wa sushi desu

tips: すきな たべもの = favourite food, literally "liked food". な joins すき to the noun.

learn.title: What is this?
learn.jp: これは なんですか？
learn.intro: Point at anything and ask. This is the question you need most in Japan, and the pattern is the same one as the hobby question.

rule.label: What is ○○?
rule.pattern: ○○は なんですか？ ／ これは なんですか？ ／ これは どういう いみですか？
rule.note: なん before です; なに on its own. どういう いみ = what meaning.

learn.when: Shops, menus, signs, lessons. Also これは いくらですか (how much) and これは どんな ○○ですか (what kind).

examples.jp: これは なんですか？
これは どういう いみですか？
examples.romaji: kore wa douiu imi desu ka?

examples.jp: これは どんな おんがくですか？
examples.romaji: kore wa donna ongaku desu ka?
examples.en: What kind of music is this?

examples.jp: これは いくらですか？

tips: Learn the question words as a set: なん what, どれ which, いくら how much, どんな what kind, どう how.

learn.title: Asking back
learn.intro: A conversation needs the question to come back. Name + さんは？ does it in two words.

rule.label: How about you?
rule.note: Use the person's name with さん. あなたは？ exists but sounds blunt; Japanese people avoid "you".

learn.when: After every answer you give. げんきです。ゆうやさんは？

examples.en: And you? (rarely used — say Name + さんは？ instead)

tips: さん goes on other people's names, never your own.

learn.title: Do you have any questions?
learn.jp: しつもんは ありますか？
learn.intro: あります means "there is" or "I have". It's the verb your teacher uses to close a lesson, so know the answers.

rule.label: Have / don't have
rule.pattern: なにか しつもんは ありますか？ → はい、あります。 ／ いいえ、ありません。
rule.note: ありますか asks; あります yes; ありません no. なにか = something, anything.

learn.when: End of every lesson. Also any "is there…?" question later on.

examples.jp: なにか しつもんは ありますか？

tips: ません is the polite negative ending for any verb: あります → ありません, わかります → わかりません.

options: よろしく おねがいします

よろしく おねがいします closes the introduction.

なん = what.

build.why: もくひょう (goal) は にほんりょこう (Japan trip) です.
あります = there is / I have.
ありません = there isn't / I don't have.
Name + さんは？ asks back.

lessons.title: Likes, dislikes & is not
lessons.goal: I can say what I like and don't like, ask others, and say what something is not.
decks: Saying “is not” · じゃないです

learn.title: I like it
learn.intro: すき is "liked" rather than "like", so the thing you like is marked with が, not を. Once you know that, every like-sentence is the same shape.

rule.label: Likes
rule.pattern: ○○が すきです。 ／ ○○が すきですか？ ／ はい、すきです。 ／ いいえ、すきじゃないです。
rule.note: が marks what is liked. Add か to ask. Deny with じゃないです, exactly like です-sentences.

learn.when: Food, music, places, anything. Answer a すきですか question with はい、すきです or いいえ、すきじゃないです.

examples.jp: いいえ、すきじゃないです。
ぼくは まぐろが すきです。
examples.romaji: boku wa maguro ga suki desu

tips: ぼくは まぐろが すきです: は for the topic (me), が for the liked thing. Both in one sentence is normal.

learn.title: What kind?
learn.jp: どんな ○○が すきですか？
learn.intro: どんな goes in front of a noun and asks for a type. It's how you move from "do you like music" to a real conversation.

rule.label: What kind of ○○
rule.pattern: どんな ○○が すきですか？
rule.note: どんな + noun. どんな おんがく = what kind of music. Answer with the type: ロックが すきです.

learn.when: After someone says they like something. Also in shops: どんな おちゃですか.

examples.jp: どんな ○○が すきですか？
examples.en: What kind of ○○ do you like?

examples.jp: どんな おんがくが すきですか？
examples.romaji: donna ongaku ga suki desu ka?
examples.en: What kind of music do you like?

examples.jp: ヒップホップと ロックが すきです。
examples.romaji: hippuhoppu to rokku ga suki desu

tips: ホラー, アクション, ヒップホップ, ロック, アニメ: genre words are mostly katakana, straight from English.

learn.title: And, too
learn.intro: Two tiny particles do a lot of work: と joins two things, も says "too".

rule.label: と and も
rule.pattern: ヒップホップと ロック ／ ぼくも ロックが すきです。
rule.note: と = and, between nouns only. も replaces は: ぼくも, not ぼくはも.

learn.when: Listing likes, agreeing with someone (ぼくも = me too).

examples.jp: ヒップホップと ロックが すきです。
examples.romaji: hippuhoppu to rokku ga suki desu

examples.jp: ぼくも ロックが すきです。
examples.romaji: boku mo rokku ga suki desu

examples.jp: にほんの れきしが すきです。
examples.romaji: nihon no rekishi ga suki desu

tips: の joins two nouns: にほんの れきし = Japanese history, literally "history of Japan".

learn.title: Saying "is not"
learn.intro: Replace です with じゃないです and any statement becomes its negative. This works for nouns, for すき, and for な-adjectives.

rule.label: The negative
rule.pattern: ○○は ▲▲です。 → ○○は ▲▲じゃないです。
rule.note: です → じゃないです. Nothing else moves. (でした is past, ですか is a question; じゃないです is the negative.)

learn.when: Correcting a wrong guess (これは すしじゃないです), saying a day isn't a work day, saying who isn't a teacher.

examples.en: It's not ○○. (です → じゃないです)

examples.jp: これは すしじゃないです。
きょうは しごとじゃないです。
きょうは やすみじゃないです。
アオイさんは せんせいじゃないです。

tips: じゃないです is the friendly polite form. You'll later meet ではありません, which is the same thing in formal writing.

learn.title: Talking about a letter
learn.intro: A small trick from your lesson: you can talk about a kana itself by putting it in 「」 brackets.

rule.label: Quoting a character
rule.pattern: これは「わ」です。 ／ これは「わ」じゃないです。
rule.note: 「」 are Japanese quotation marks. Useful for the look-alike kana drills.

learn.when: Checking you've read a kana right: これは「あ」ですか？

examples.jp: これは「わ」じゃないです。

tips: ね, れ and わ look alike. Use this pattern to check: これは「ね」ですか？

learn.title: Things you don't like
learn.jp: なっとうが すきじゃないです
learn.intro: Disliking something politely uses the negative of すき, not a separate word. It's softer than English "I hate".

rule.label: Don't like
rule.pattern: ○○が すきじゃないです。
rule.note: There is a word きらい (dislike), but すきじゃない is what people actually say.

learn.when: Food you won't eat, music you'd rather skip.

examples.jp: なっとうが すきじゃないです。
いいえ、すきじゃないです。

tips: なっとう (fermented soybeans) is the classic test. Most visitors don't like it, and Japanese people expect you to say so.

vocab: ヒップホップ ／ ロック
ホラー ／ アクション
ラーメン ／ コーヒー

build.why: が marks the thing that is liked.
Add か to ask.
Negative of すきです = すきじゃないです.

build.en: What kind of music do you like?
build.jp: ___ おんがくが すきですか？
build.why: どんな + noun = what kind of.

build.jp: ヒップホップ___ ロックが すきです。
build.why: と = and, between two nouns.

build.jp: ぼく___ ロックが すきです。
build.why: も = too. It replaces は.

build.jp: にほん___ れきしが すきです。
build.why: の = of / 's. にほんの れきし = Japan's history.
が marks natto, then the negative of すき.

lessons.title: This one, which one & prices
lessons.goal: I can point at things with これ・それ・あれ, ask which one, count to 100, and understand prices in yen.

learn.title: This, that, that over there
learn.intro: English has this and that. Japanese has three, chosen by where the thing is: near me, near you, or away from both of us.

rule.label: Three distances
rule.pattern: これ near me ／ それ near you ／ あれ over there ／ どれ which one
rule.note: こ・そ・あ・ど is a system: the same first sounds appear in ここ・そこ・あそこ・どこ (here, there, over there, where).

learn.when: Pointing at things in shops and restaurants. In doubt, これ + pointing.

examples.jp: これ ／ それ ／ あれ
examples.en: this (near me) / that (near you) / that (over there)

examples.jp: これは いくらですか？
それは いくらですか？

tips: それ is the one near the person you're talking to, so それは いくらですか asks about the thing the staff member is holding.

learn.title: Which one?
learn.intro: どれ asks which one out of three or more. Put the thing you're looking for first, then は どれですか.

rule.label: Which one is ○○?
rule.pattern: ○○は どれですか？ ／ あおい せんすは どれですか？
rule.note: Adjective before the noun, no particle: あおい せんす (blue fan). Then は どれですか.

learn.when: A shelf of similar things, a menu, a row of fans.

examples.jp: あおい せんすは どれですか？
examples.romaji: aoi sensu wa dore desu ka?
examples.en: Which one is the blue fan?

examples.jp: ひだり ／ まんなか ／ みぎ

tips: The answer is often a direction: ひだり (left), まんなか (middle), みぎ (right). ひだりです = it's the left one.

learn.title: Counting to 100
learn.intro: Ten numbers, then stacking. Twenty-one is "two-ten-one". Three numbers have a second reading; learn the safe one.

rule.label: Stacking
rule.pattern: じゅういち = 11 ／ にじゅう = 20 ／ にじゅういち = 21 ／ きゅうじゅうきゅう = 99
rule.note: Use よん (4), なな (7), きゅう (9). し, しち and く exist but are avoided: し sounds like "death".

learn.when: Prices, ages, dates, phone numbers, your room number.
tips: ゼロ ／ れい are both zero. ゼロ is the borrowed word, れい the native one; either works.

learn.title: Hundreds and thousands
learn.intro: ひゃく is 100, せん is 1,000. Stack a number in front, but five combinations change their sound to be easier to say.

rule.label: Sound changes
rule.pattern: さんびゃく 300 ／ ろっぴゃく 600 ／ はっぴゃく 800 ／ さんぜん 3,000 ／ はっせん 8,000
rule.note: Everything else is regular: にひゃく, よんひゃく, ななひゃく, きゅうひゃく, にせん, ろくせん.

learn.when: Every price in Japan. A coffee is around よんひゃくえん, a fan around はっぴゃくえん.

examples.jp: にひゃく ごじゅう
ひだりは はっぴゃく えんです。

tips: Say the five changed ones out loud ten times: さんびゃく, ろっぴゃく, はっぴゃく, さんぜん, はっせん. They're the whole trick.

learn.title: Ten thousand: まん
learn.intro: This is the one that trips up every English speaker. Japanese counts big numbers in ten-thousands, not thousands.

rule.label: The まん system
rule.note: 10,000 is NEVER じゅうせん. A new word starts: まん. Then stack below it: いちまん ごせん = 1 まん + 5 せん.

learn.when: Hotels, train passes, nicer souvenirs. A yukata might be にまんえん.

examples.jp: みぎは にまん えんです。

examples.en: 10,000 is NOT じゅうせん → always いちまん

tips: To convert: cut the number four digits from the right. 20,000 → 2 | 0000 → にまん. 15,000 → 1 | 5000 → いちまん ごせん.

learn.title: Reacting to a price
learn.intro: Once you can hear a price, react to it. やすい is cheap; it's an い-adjective, so it takes です and ね like the others.

rule.label: Cheap!
rule.pattern: やすいですね！
rule.note: ね again: "that's cheap, isn't it!". The opposite, たかい (expensive), comes later.

learn.when: A good price. Say it with a smile; it's a compliment to the shop.

examples.jp: これは いくらですか？

tips: Ask → hear the number → react. That's a complete shop exchange in three lines.

lessons.title: Shopping in Asakusa
lessons.goal: I can ask what something is and how much it costs at a shop in Asakusa, and buy it with ～を ください.

learn.title: How was your day?
learn.jp: きょうは どうでしたか？
learn.intro: Your teacher opens every lesson with this. The trick is to have one short answer ready, and the answer uses a new idea: adjectives in Japanese carry their own past tense.

rule.label: Past tense of い-adjectives
rule.pattern: いそがしい → いそがしかったです
rule.note: Drop the final い, add かった. Then です just makes it polite. Never say いそがしいでした.

learn.when: Any time someone asks how your day, weekend or lesson was. One sentence is enough.

examples.jp: きょうは どうでしたか？
しごとが いそがしかったです。
ジムは たのしかったです。

tips: You already know よかったです (it was good). Same rule: よい → よかった.
Rhythm: きょ・う・は・ど・う・で・し・た・か is nine beats. Give every beat the same length, and keep the す in です quiet.

learn.title: What will you do this weekend?
learn.jp: しゅうまつ、なにを しますか？
learn.intro: Japanese has no separate future tense. ます covers both "I do" and "I will do", so ジムに いきます is "I'll go to the gym" when you're talking about the weekend.

rule.label: Going somewhere
rule.pattern: PLACE に いきます
rule.note: に marks the place you go to. を marks the thing you do something to, as in なにを しますか.

learn.when: Plans. Add a time word at the front: しゅうまつ (weekend), あした (tomorrow), きょう (today).

examples.jp: しゅうまつ、なにを しますか？
examples.en: What will you do this weekend?

examples.jp: しゅうまつ、ジムに いきます。
examples.en: I'll go to the gym this weekend.

examples.jp: あした、しごとに いきます。

tips: いきました (I went) is the past. You used ジムに いきました last lesson: ます → ました.

learn.title: The core sentence: X は Y です
learn.intro: This is the most basic sentence in Japanese, and you already use it constantly: げんきです, しごとです, おちゃです. Everything in this lesson is one of three versions of it.

rule.label: Three versions
rule.note: is / is not / is it? To make a question, just add か at the end. は as a particle is read "wa".

learn.when: Saying what something is, denying it, or asking. Answer a ですか question with はい + です or いいえ + じゃないです.

examples.jp: きょうは しごとですか？
あしたは しごとですか？
いいえ、しごとじゃないです。
これは おちゃじゃないです。コーヒーです。
examples.romaji: kore wa ocha janai desu. koohii desu

tips: The answer echoes the question. しごとですか？ → しごとです。 You don't need a word for "yes I do"; the pattern does it.
Ask back with Name + さんは？ to keep a conversation going: はい、げんきです。ゆうやさんは？ Avoid あなたは; it sounds blunt.

learn.title: What is it? Which one is it?
learn.jp: なんですか・どれですか
learn.intro: Two questions you'll use in every shop in Japan. Both are the X は ▲▲ですか pattern with a question word in the ▲▲ slot.

rule.label: Question words in the slot
rule.pattern: ○○は なんですか？ ／ ○○は どれですか？ ／ ○○は いくらですか？
rule.note: What is ○○? / Which one is ○○? / How much is ○○? Just swap the question word.

learn.when: どれ when there are three or more things to choose from. Point and use これ when you don't know the item's name.

examples.jp: しゅみは なんですか？
おちゃは どれですか？
おみやげは どれですか？
これは なんですか？……これは いくらですか？
examples.romaji: kore wa nan desu ka? ... kore wa ikura desu ka?
examples.en: What is this? ... How much is this?

tips: Challenge from your teacher: ask two in a row. What is it, then how much. That's a full shop interaction.

learn.title: At a shop
learn.intro: The December goal: walk into a shop in Asakusa, ask what something is and how much, and buy it. Here are the four lines you need, plus what the staff will say to you.

rule.label: Buying something
rule.pattern: ITEM を ください。
rule.note: "ITEM, please" or "I'll take ITEM". を marks what you're asking for. ITEM を おねがいします is the softer, more polite version.

learn.when: いらっしゃいませ is what staff say when you walk in. You don't answer it; a nod or こんにちは is fine. Then ask, then buy.

examples.jp: あかい おちゃを ください。
おちゃを おねがいします。
とても きれいですね。

tips: ね at the end invites agreement: きれいですね is "it's beautiful, isn't it?". Staff will love it.
Adjective before the noun, no particle: あかい おちゃ (red tea), あおい せんす (blue fan).
Prices you'll hear: せんえん 1,000, にせんえん 2,000, さんびゃくえん 300, はっぴゃくえん 800.

learn.title: Hiragana that look alike
learn.jp: にている ひらがな
learn.intro: Your teacher noticed you mixing up あ, お and め. Everyone does at first. The fix is to know exactly where to look.

rule.label: Look at the top first
rule.pattern: あ = cross + big loop ／ お = cross + loop + dot ／ め = no cross ／ ぬ = め + curl
rule.note: Is there a cross (十) at the top? Then look for the dot on the right.

learn.when: Reading menus and shop signs. あと means "after"; あとめ is not a word.

examples.en: red (not めかい: あ has the cross)
souvenir (not あみやげ: お has the dot)
sushi (not すじ: the two small marks change し to じ)

tips: き has two lines at the top, さ has one.
ね curls at the end, れ kicks out, わ is round.

たのしい → たのしかった. です stays the same.
に marks the place you go to.
